objective: Test whether Git object identity plus a separately retained SHA can provide a zero-cost non-rollbackable freshness witness across branch rewind, repository delete/recreate same-name reuse, unreachable-object retention uncertainty, response loss, rate-limit interruption and later retry, without silently introducing another durable recovery domain.

public_sources.observation: The Git overview describes repository objects as named by a hash of their contents and refs as named pointers to object identities. This supports content-address identity/authenticity reasoning, not freshness by itself.

git-prune explicitly removes unreachable objects from the object database, subject to reachability/expiry rules. Therefore an unreachable object identity is not a generic permanent retention guarantee.

git-gc documents repository housekeeping that can remove unreachable objects and notes automatic maintenance plus configurable pruning. This supports treating unreachable-object survival as uncertain rather than durable anti-rollback memory.

finite_model.decision_goal: Accept useful current g1 in legitimately-old histories while rejecting or refusing g1 after a hidden g2 existed and the repository-visible authority rolled back. A rate-limit trace may checkpoint/refuse in this invocation and retry later; no same-run retry is counted.
finite_model.collision_scope: Cryptographic hash collision attacks are outside this bounded model; the tested question is rollback/freshness, not collision resistance.

current_ref_hash_only.finding: Current content/object identity authenticates the visible state but contains no memory that a newer state previously existed.

same_repo_pointer_or_anchor.finding: A witness stored only inside the same rollback/delete-recreate domain rolls back or disappears with that domain in this tested adversarial event.

external_bare_sha_conservative.finding: A surviving bare SHA can distinguish identity when it survives elsewhere, but a mismatch is not itself an ordering proof. When the newer object is unavailable or the compare is rate-limited, the safe action is refusal/checkpoint. Its durable survival is already a third recovery domain.

external_generation_sha_record.finding: A surviving generation+SHA record can carry freshness even after object loss, but only because generation metadata and the SHA survived in an independent durable domain.

combined_fail_closed_external_witness.finding: Safety is obtainable by using surviving external witness material and refusing when proof is absent, but this is not generic useful-outcome parity and does not eliminate the independent durable-domain requirement.

indistinguishability.pair_definition: For each rollback_event x newer_object_state x transport x witness in {none,same_repo_pointer}, the visible current-domain observation is identical between legit_old_g1 and advanced_g2_then_rollback_to_g1.
indistinguishability.consequence: Any deterministic mechanism restricted to that current rollback domain must either accept both worlds (unsafe after rollback) or refuse both worlds (safe but not useful in the legitimate-old world).

separation.content_address_authenticity: If object bytes are available, the retained hash can identify the expected content/object under this non-collision model.
separation.discoverability_reachability: A hash must be remembered somewhere and the object must remain fetchable/reachable/retained to recover object-graph relations. Git documents pruning of unreachable objects, so unreachable-object survival is not a generic permanent guarantee.
separation.freshness_anti_rollback: A bare hash has no intrinsic generation order. Freshness requires surviving ordering metadata, an ancestry relation that can still be checked, or another non-rollbackable witness.

response_loss_and_rate_limit.response_loss: Does not create independent anti-rollback memory. The safe model preserves idempotent refusal/checkpoint unless a surviving witness already proves freshness.
response_loss_and_rate_limit.rate_limit: No same-run retry. The current effect is refused/checkpointed and the comparison is retried in a later invocation under a fresh bootstrap; this preserves safety but does not solve witness absence.

phase1_result.new_narrowing: Immutable Git object identity is an authenticity/addressing primitive, not self-remembering anti-rollback state. Keeping a newer SHA in the same rollback domain does not survive common-mode rewind/delete-recreate; keeping it outside that domain explicitly introduces the third durable recovery domain Part131 already identified. Bare SHA survival also does not by itself encode newer-than ordering when object ancestry is unavailable.
phase1_result.exact_tested_scope: The stated 144 finite traces plus the cited Git object/ref/pruning semantics. This does not prove GitHub-specific retention durations, deletion restoration guarantees, cryptographic collision resistance, arbitrary Byzantine safety, or provider-level repository-incarnation fencing.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.richer_mode_protected_manual_execution_d: none for the finite model itself; any accepted anti-rollback design that relies on externally retained SHA/generation metadata still has an unresolved independent durable recovery-domain dependency
zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_transport: lightweight state/evidence transport only; rate-limit interruption is checkpointed across invocations

unresolved_children: A zero-cost Chat-native non-rollbackable recovery witness independent of repository+sink common-mode rollback remains unproven.
A bare retained SHA requires both durable survival and enough surviving ordering/ancestry information to establish freshness; otherwise it is identity-only evidence.
Same-repository unreachable-object retention is not a generic permanent guarantee because unreachable objects can be pruned.
Part128 repository-incarnation write-time fencing remains unresolved and is now the highest-value direct child.
continuation: Part133: execute one bounded repository-incarnation write-time fencing leaf. Hold Parts128-132 fixed. Test whether a provider-stable repository identity (for example repository ID/node identity), current contents/blob CAS preconditions, and lightweight repository APIs can prevent a stale pre-delete client from committing into a delete/recreate same-name repository without requiring a separately durable remembered old incarnation token. Include same-name reuse, stale blob SHA collision-of-name but not content, create-versus-update paths, response loss, rate-limit interruption and later retry. Separate server-enforced target identity from client-retained incarnation memory. Any scheme that requires remembering the prior repository ID/token in another durable domain must count that dependency explicitly. Use only own clean state and public sources; no hosted compute/coordinator/finite quota/manual execution. Absence of a generic fence remains an unresolved child, not closure.
